summary: 1938 40-foot pole L-4 lookout near the Canadian border in Pend Oreille County; now gone, with a footing reportedly still visible.

facts.design: 40-foot pole tower with an L-4 cab
facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say gone; a Washington lookout list marks it removed. No removal date in the sources read. WillhiteWeb's 2024 description reports a footing still visible.

access.note: On Colville National Forest land. A gate on the access road is closed December 1 to July 1 for wildlife habitat. The final few hundred feet are a bushwhack. No current closure notice found in the sources read.

visit.trail_note: No tower stands. WillhiteWeb's route starts on Highway 31 north of Metaline Falls, runs up Slumber Mountain Road and forest roads FR 400 and 430, then a bushwhack. Hike is about 1.3 miles one way.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 5,140 feet (1,567 m); WillhiteWeb gives 5,120 feet. The story reports the register figure and WillhiteWeb's figure side by side.

notes_for_editor: Brief's access 'unknown' is set to restricted from the gate and bushwhack described by WillhiteWeb; the seasonal gate is the only access limit in the sources, so confirm before publishing the access line. Height 12.2 m is converted from the 40-foot figure. Brief's lat/lon matches the register's degree-minute coordinates; the West US Lookouts coordinates in the brief differ by about half a kilometre and were not used. No staffing, fire history or removal date found in the sources read. Story is built, fate and today only.
